info.title: DEP real-time plane
info.description:
The real-time plane of the Document Editing Protocol 1.0 (draft), generated from packages/protocol/src/definition (05 §4, §5; SPK-019, PRO-001).

This document describes a DEP server: `receive` operations are messages a client sends, `send` operations are messages the server sends; `both` messages have one of each.

One multiplexed WebSocket with the subprotocol `dep.v1`. Each text frame is one JSON object, the envelope `{ t, id, re, ch, d }`. Binary frames are reserved for engines with opaque payloads (three unsigned LEB128 integers `ch`, `kind`, `id`, then the payload); `pm-steps/1` does not use them.

Receivers MUST ignore fields and message types they do not know; a message of an unknown type that carries an `id` is answered with `error` `unknown_type`, `fatal: false` (05 §1 rule 3).

Gaps and decisions are referenced by identifier (`x-dep-gaps`, `x-dep-decisions`, `$comment`); spec/dep/dep-1.gaps.json lists them.

dep.title: DEP WebSocket
dep.description: The `ws` address announced in discovery (05 §2). The `Origin` header is checked against the tenant's allowed origins when `hello` arrives.

host.description: Host of the `ws` address from discovery.

path.description: Path of the `ws` address from discovery.

dep.title: DEP connection
dep.description: The whole connection: session messages and every channel multiplexed by `ch`. Messages on one channel are delivered in order; there is no ordering between channels. At most one channel per document may be open on a connection.

Sec-WebSocket-Protocol.description: The subprotocol carries the major version (05 §1 rule 1, §4).

x-dep-close-codes.meaning: No common protocol version. The preceding error lists the server's versions

receive.hello.title: Receive hello
receive.hello.summary: Opens the session. Must be the first message, within 10 seconds.

receive.auth.refresh.title: Receive auth.refresh
receive.auth.refresh.summary: Presents a new token; with `ch`, a token for that channel.

send.auth.ok.title: Send auth.ok
send.auth.ok.summary: Reply to `auth.refresh`: the refreshed token is accepted.

send.auth.revoked.title: Send auth.revoked
send.auth.revoked.summary: The session was revoked; followed by close code 4401.

receive.ping.title: Receive ping
receive.ping.summary: Sent after `heartbeatMs` without sending anything; the peer answers `pong`.

send.ping.title: Send ping
send.ping.summary: Sent after `heartbeatMs` without sending anything; the peer answers `pong`.

send.goaway.title: Send goaway
send.goaway.summary: The whole connection is draining; never used for a single channel.

receive.error.title: Receive error
receive.error.summary: A typed error; with `re` when it answers a message. A fatal error is followed by the matching close code.

send.error.title: Send error
send.error.summary: A typed error; with `re` when it answers a message. A fatal error is followed by the matching close code.

receive.chunk.title: Receive chunk
receive.chunk.summary: One part of a message whose UTF-8 size exceeds `maxMessageBytes`; chunks of one message are sent consecutively; reassembly times out after 10 seconds.

send.chunk.title: Send chunk
send.chunk.summary: One part of a message whose UTF-8 size exceeds `maxMessageBytes`; chunks of one message are sent consecutively; reassembly times out after 10 seconds.

receive.ch.open.title: Receive ch.open
receive.ch.open.summary: Opens a document channel. Without `resume` the server answers with `catchUp: "reload"`.

send.ch.opened.title: Send ch.opened
send.ch.opened.summary: The channel is attached; `head` is the durable head at that moment.

send.ch.rejected.title: Send ch.rejected
send.ch.rejected.summary: The channel could not be opened.

send.ch.closed.title: Send ch.closed
send.ch.closed.summary: The server closed a channel, for example `forbidden` after revocation, `unavailable` when the room moves or is fenced, `slow_consumer`. Under read restrictions (ADR 0019, proposed) a change of access that hides or reveals content also closes the channel with `unavailable`, and the next open reloads.

receive.sync.submit.title: Receive sync.submit
receive.sync.submit.summary: Submits a commit. The envelope `id` correlates the reply; the payload `id` identifies the commit.

send.sync.ack.title: Send sync.ack
send.sync.ack.summary: The commit is stored; sent only after every commit with a lower `seq` on the channel.

send.sync.reject.title: Send sync.reject
send.sync.reject.summary: The commit was refused; `action` says what to do next and `head` is the current head.

send.sync.commit.title: Send sync.commit
send.sync.commit.summary: Stored commits, in ascending `seq`; the next message continues at the last `seq` plus one.

send.sync.caughtUp.title: Send sync.caughtUp
send.sync.caughtUp.summary: The catch-up stream is complete; live commits follow.

send.sync.reset.title: Send sync.reset
send.sync.reset.summary: A snapshot commit was stored; the client reloads content at `seq`.

send.sync.check.title: Send sync.check
send.sync.check.summary: The SHA-256 of the canonical form of the document at `seq`, for divergence detection (04 §13).

receive.presence.update.title: Receive presence.update
receive.presence.update.summary: Publishes the client's selection; positions refer to the confirmed document at `seq`.

send.presence.state.title: Send presence.state
send.presence.state.summary: Peers and sessions that left. The server adds identity and MAY drop or coalesce presence under load.

send.perm.changed.title: Send perm.changed
send.perm.changed.summary: A complete new `access` object. The server enforces it from the moment it computes it.

send.event.title: Send event
send.event.summary: "This changed; fetch it over REST if you care."

send.wf.changed.title: Send wf.changed
send.wf.changed.summary: The workflow state and the participant's status; sent like `perm.changed`.

Envelope.title: Envelope
Envelope.description: Every text frame is one JSON object. Receivers MUST ignore members they do not know, and ignore message types they do not know (05 §1 rule 3).

id.description: Set by the sender on a message that expects a reply.

re.description: The `id` this message replies to. Required on every reply.

ch.description: Channel number, on every channel-scoped message including `ch.open`.

DocRole.title: DocRole
DocRole.description: A document-level role, carried in the `docs` claim (05 §3.1; 07 §2).

Restriction.title: Restriction
Restriction.description: An output restriction from the `restrict` claim (05 §3.1; 13 §5).

ScopeId.title: ScopeId
ScopeId.description: A scope identifier: `doc`, `body`, `defs`, `region:<id>`, `story:<id>` or `field:<id>` (05 §5.3), where `<id>` is a node identifier.

FeatureName.title: FeatureName
FeatureName.description: A feature name. Protocol and CDM features share one namespace; experimental names start with `x-` (05 §1).

ScopeCapability.title: ScopeCapability
ScopeCapability.description: A capability held in one scope: a capability of 07 §1, or `structure.add` on the scope `defs` (a grant that lists `defs.add`; ADR 0424).

ScopeCapabilities.title: ScopeCapabilities
ScopeCapabilities.description: A set of capabilities held in one scope.

holder.description: The user who holds the lease: the host's `sub` (D42).

expiresAt.description: When the lease ends unless it is extended.

active.description: Whether the participant is active in the workflow.

Access.title: Access
Access.description: Effective access, sent in `ch.opened` and as the whole payload of `perm.changed` (05 §5.5).

rev.description: Access revision of this connection; it increases whenever anything that feeds effective permissions changes.

asOfSeq.description: The sequence number whose region list this access describes.

scopes.description: Capabilities per scope. A region scope holds `structure` where a grant lists `region.retitle`; `defs` holds `structure.add` where one lists `defs.add` (ADR 0424). Lists every region of the document; a region not listed is not editable until an access with `asOfSeq` at or after the commit that created it arrives.

fill.description: Fill permission, or null when it does not apply (12 §4.1).

restrictions.description: Output restrictions; empty when none apply.

Step.title: Step
Step.description: A step as produced by `Step.toJSON()` of the pinned prosemirror-transform release (04 §4). Validated by the authority, not by the envelope.

stepType.description: The step type. The authority accepts only the seven known types and rejects any other with `invalid_op` (04 §4), so the wire format accepts any string.

Origin.title: Origin
Origin.description: Origin of a commit: a client hint (recorded, never trusted) or a server-reserved origin (04 §3.1).

Commit.title: Commit
Commit.description: A step commit as submitted: the payload of `sync.submit` (04 §3.1; 05 §5.3).

id.description: Commit identifier chosen by the client; reused unchanged when the same commit is resubmitted.

base.description: The `seq` the client had applied when it created the steps.

Ack.title: Ack
Ack.description: The payload of `sync.ack` (05 §5.3; 04 §7). `re` is the envelope `id` of the submit.

id.description: The commit identifier.

serverTime.description: Server time of the commit (04 G6).

rebased.description: Whether the steps were rebased. Always true for a read-restricted reader, whose acknowledgement carries the steps of its class (ADR 0019, proposed).

steps.description: The mapped steps: required when `rebased` is true; an acknowledgement rebuilt for a duplicate always carries them.

QuotaKind.title: QuotaKind
QuotaKind.description: The kind of quota a refusal names: the dimensions of the tenant quotas (06 §12; owner decision 110).

SyncReject.title: SyncReject
SyncReject.description: The payload of `sync.reject` (05 §5.3; 04 §8). A commit whose base is older than a snapshot commit gets `stale_base` with action `rebase` (04 §3.2).

id.description: The commit identifier from the submit (it may be malformed, which is why it is not typed as a UUID).

code.description: A registry code with the sync surface.

scopes.description: Scopes involved, for `permission_denied`; never a scope the reader may not see.

rule.description: The rule or constraint that failed (12 §5.3).

retryAfterMs.description: How long to wait before retrying.

quota.description: For `quota_exceeded` and a spent room CPU budget: the kind of quota reached (owner decision 110).

Author.title: Author
Author.description: Server attribution of a commit (04 G6).

user.description: The user the commit is attributed to: the host's `sub` (D42), or `system` (04 §10).

session.description: The session; null for server-authored commits.

agent.description: The assistant that acted for the user, or null (13 §6.2).

ControlChange.title: ControlChange
ControlChange.description: The change a control commit records (04 §3.2). Only `{ "type": "grants", "rev": n }` appears in the prose.

type.description: What changed (04 §3.2 lists grants revisions, region states, lease breaks, workflow transitions and participant completion).

RemoteCommit.title: RemoteCommit
RemoteCommit.description: A stored commit as broadcast in `sync.commit` (05 §5.3).

steps.description: The steps as applied; empty for a control commit. For a read-restricted reader, the steps of its class, which are empty when the commit changed only hidden content (ADR 0019, proposed).

control.description: The change a control commit records; null for a step commit.

Resume.title: Resume
Resume.description: Where a client resumes a channel (05 §5.2; 04 §9).

incarnation.description: The log incarnation the `seq` belongs to.

view.description: The `view` of the `ch.opened` the confirmed document came from (ADR 0019, proposed). Under read restrictions a missing or different token forces `catchUp: "reload"`.

Inflight.title: Inflight
Inflight.description: The fate of the in-flight commit named in `resume` (04 §9).

seq.description: The `seq` of the stored commit, when accepted.

CatchUp.title: CatchUp
CatchUp.description: How a joining client catches up (05 §5.2).

Limits.title: Limits
Limits.description: Every limit a client must respect (05 §5.1).

maxMessageBytes.description: Largest UTF-8 size of one frame; larger messages are chunked.

maxRebaseSteps.description: Most steps a commit may be rebased over (default 5,000, 04 §5).

heartbeatMs.description: Idle interval after which a side sends `ping` (default 25,000).

ackTimeoutMs.description: How long a client waits for an answer to a submit (default 15,000, 04 §8).

presenceHz.description: Most presence updates per second per client (default 10, 04 §11).

catchUpBytes.description: Most bytes streamed on resume (default 5 MiB, 04 §9).

CdmRange.title: CdmRange
CdmRange.description: A range of CDM major versions (05 §2).

id.description: The user identifier: the token's `sub` (D42).

name.description: Display name, when the token has a `name` claim.

quota.description: For `quota_exceeded` and a spent room CPU budget: the kind of quota reached (owner decision 110).

fatal.description: A fatal error is followed by the matching close code (05 §5.7).

versions.description: The server's versions, in the error before close 4406.

head.description: The durable head when the channel was attached; the first live commit is `head + 1`.

view.description: An opaque token naming the visibility class (the projection for this reader) that the content and stream of the channel belong to (ADR 0019, proposed). A client echoes it in a later resume.

WorkflowStatus.title: WorkflowStatus
WorkflowStatus.description: The workflow state and the participant's status, carried by `wf.changed` and `ch.opened.workflow` (12 §6.2, §10).

state.description: The participant's own status: `active` (may act now), `unverified` (their turn, but the access code is still to be submitted), `waiting` (an earlier order first), `completed`, `paused` (while correcting), `closed` (the workflow ended), or `copy` (a `cc` participant). Never another participant's.

Notification.title: Notification
Notification.description: The payload of `event`: "this changed; fetch it over REST if you care" (05 §5.6).

resource.description: The resource that changed, relative to `rest`.

data.description: Small data; thread events carry the thread's current range and the `seq` it refers to.

PresenceState.title: PresenceState
PresenceState.description: What a client publishes about itself (05 §5.4).

selection.description: Positions in the confirmed document at `seq`.

PresencePeer.title: PresencePeer
PresencePeer.description: A peer in `presence.state`; the server adds identity (05 §5.4).

NotificationType.title: NotificationType
NotificationType.description: Notification type: an open vocabulary; a client ignores types it does not know (05 §1 rule 3).

token.description: The user token (a JWT, 05 §3.1). Tokens are never placed in URLs.

session.description: A new identifier for every connection; there is no session resumption.

of.description: A fresh identifier shared by the chunks of one message.

part.description: A substring of the serialised message, split only between Unicode code points.

cdm.description: The CDM version the client will use.

token.description: A token for this channel; same `tid` and `sub` as the session (05 §3.1).

cause.description: Why the server closed the channel. `access_changed`: what the reader may see changed (ADR 0019), so the client reopens without `resume`; the others say why a room stopped serving, and the client resumes as for `unavailable`.
